title: 3 Anime to Watch If You Love Sword Art Online
content:
It’s been more than six years since Sword Art Online released its second season, and the next installment is going to be its anticipated feature-length movie. However, the movie will only be released in 2028, and fans in the U.S. will have to wait even longer for its global premiere. Based on the critically acclaimed light novel written by Reki Kawahara and illustrated by BUNBUN, Sword Art Online made its anime debut in 2012 and became a massive hit. Over the years, the anime has released three seasons, three theatrical movies, anime extras, and even spin-offs. The franchise is still standing stronger than ever as fans are eagerly awaiting updates on the upcoming movie, Sword Art Online Movie: Integral Domain .

It’s too soon for the movie to share its full trailer and release dates, but fans already know it’s going to be another banger. The movie will follow the original story concept written by series creator Reki Kawahara and is set after the Alicization arc. Although the wait for the anime’s return is longer than ever, there are several exciting anime fans can watch in the meantime to fill the void. If you’re looking for anime with similar vibes to this classic fantasy, we’ve got you covered.

3) Accel World

If you aren’t already familiar with Kawahara’s other works, Accel World will be a great starting point. The creator has written a few light novels over the years, out of which three have already received anime adaptations. Accel World has the same video game world-building and the intense moments that fans of Sword Art Online will immediately fall in love with. Unfortunately, even though this anime was released in 2012, it never received the attention it deserved. The story centers around Haruyuki Arita, a middle school student who has always been bullied for his weight.

He finds solace in playing online games, but his life takes a drastic turn after he encounters the school’s vice president of the student council, Kuroyukihime, who will surpass all his high scores. She also introduces him to Brain Burst, a program that not only allows its users to accelerate their brain waves, but it also functions as an augmented reality fighting game. Kuroyukihime requests his assistance to get to the top, something Haruyuki finds it difficult to refuse, especially after she helped him overcome the bullies that tormented him.

2) Grimgar, Ashes and Illusions

This underrated isekai never received enough popularity to return with a second season. Although there’s no denying that the first season is an incredible journey regardless of the fact that there’s no anime continuation. This is yet another survival game where a group of people has been thrown into a world of fantasy that they can’t escape from. The survival anime follows a group of strangers who wake up in a mysterious fantasy world with no memories of their past lives.

Unlike the generic isekai shows where the reincarnated or transmigrated characters adapt to their new surroundings quickly, this anime doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal reality of being powerless and unprepared in a completely unknown world. It’s a story of survival as it follows ordinary people who have been thrust into a dangerous world where they must fight monsters for food and money. Their struggles are visceral and slow-paced, emphasizing the weight of every decision while the characters try their best to come out of this dangerous world alive.

1) Devils’ Crest

This is the newest anime from the creator of Sword Art Online , and it premiered in November 2026. The anime is still ongoing, so you can easily catch up with the episodes in no time. While the series is fairly new, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say it’s easily one of the best anime of the year. It has a much darker tone than Kawahara’s most popular work. Not to mention that instead of the characters being trapped in a video game, Devils’ Crest blends the virtual reality into the real world, making the situation more horrifying than anything.

The story follows sixth-grade students Yuma Ashihara and his twin sister Sawa. While playing a brand-new virtual reality MMORPG, they realize that their world is being fused with the game. It doesn’t take long for the situation to turn from bad to worse as death keeps lurking around every corner, causing chaos and confusion among others. What’s worse is that someone Yuma personally knows undergoes a terrible metamorphosis and turns into one of the game’s horrifying monsters.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to Sword Art Online ? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Addresses Divisive Changes to Art Style & Animation
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens has a much different look to it than fans saw with the previous Avatar: The Last Airbender outings, and one of the producers behind it all has addressed why the series has been changed so much with its art style and animation techniques. Avatar: Seven Havens is a sort of clean break from the rest of the franchise as it takes place hundreds of years after the events of The Legend of Korra . And that comes with a drastic change in the way it’s designed its world too.

Avatar: Seven Havens executive producer Ethan Spaulding recently took part in a Reddit AMA for the series, and had been asked by fans why it looks so different than from what was seen in the prior series with characters having larger eyes and different proportions. As Spaulding explained, this was due to Avatar: Seven Havens being imagined with a “more obvious anime style ” as the team was going for a more fantasy based look for its world.

Why Avatar: Seven Havens Has Such Different Anime Designs

“With all of the Avatar properties there is always a change in look and style , Seven Havens was always imagined as having a more obvious anime style to its characters,” Spaulding explained. “We were going for a more fantasy based look and it being a Post Cataclysmic world this aesthetic choice seemed a good fit.” When it comes to the actual animation of the series, Spaulding noted that the team wanted to lean into the “limited” style seen in other anime releases with plans to save it for the bigger moments.

“The decision was to lean into ‘limited animation’ as anime does and have fuller animation when the scenes really called for it, and yes time and budget is always a consideration in a tv series,” Spaulding revealed. For those fans questioning the series’ fluidity, Spaulding also stated, “The animation keeps getting better and better as the series progresses.” That has already been seen with episodes like the first season’s final few, and that’s likely going to be case with the bigger episodes coming in the future.

Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Teases Big Finales in the Future

“The Bigger tentpole finale episodes do get a bigger budget and also it is natural as a new series progresses,” Spaulding also revealed when asked if the bigger episodes do get a more sizable budget. The producer also noted that “the animation gets better and better as animators become more familiar with animating the designs.” Avatar: Seven Havens has been in the works for the last few years, so it’s likely that the series is going to get even bigger and better from here as Pavi heads into the other Havens .

One of the drawbacks of this first Avatar: Seven Havens was the lack of one on one fights compared to what was seen in other series, but that’s likely going to change now that the other Havens are set to be revealed. Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is going to be hitting Paramount+ next May, with Season 3 hitting in late 2027. The series will then come to an end with Season 4 , so there’s all sorts of opportunity for big moments. But how are you feeling about Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ art style and animation so far? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Crunchyroll’s Hottest Fall Anime Just Dropped the Coolest Fight of 2026
content:
Crunchyroll is featuring a lot of anime currently airing this season. However, arguably the coolest fight of this year has emerged from one of Fall 2026’s hottest anime, and no one expected it, precisely because the series’ premise does not initially incorporate action as its main element. The anime, initially dubbed the replacement for Solo Leveling this fall, Overgeared has emerged as a series of its own, delivering some of the best crafting action and now a straight-up action sequence in its latest episode that stands on the same level as major anime such as Jujutsu Kaisen , Bleach , Black Clover , and many others. The surprising element is that it comes from the studio behind One-Punch Man Seasons 2 and 3, which has been dubbed the studio that ruined a masterpiece.

Overgeared has been standing out since the start, initially thanks to its protagonist, who stands out through his desperation. With Grid’s main goal being to acquire money and his primary ability revolving around crafting, the series established itself with a different kind of protagonist and action sequences that stood out thanks to their crafting element . However, the series continued to incorporate action as well, given that combat is a core element of MMORPGs. Now, the latest episode features roughly six to seven minutes of action that matches the climactic sequences of a high-budget anime film.

Crunchyroll’s Overgeared Delivers One of the Coolest and Biggest Anime Fights of 2026

Overgeared Episode 9, titled “Comrades in the Guild,” continues the fight between Tzedakah’s guild and Malaxus, the leader of the Yatan cult, with Grid joining the raid as well. With Grid possessing the Shield of Yatan, he boosts the confidence of the guild members, and the fight begins, featuring every member playing their role. It starts with the Macho Man delivering close-combat action that is perfectly animated, offering the kind of hand-to-hand combat that the Naruto series has often showcased. Following this, two more characters appear, fighting Malaxus with a sword and a spear. This is where one of the most beautiful shots is captured, as the camera pans across the action, delivering a captivating sequence.

Following this, the characters with projectile abilities attack Malaxus one by one, with every attack visually enhanced. This culminates in the guild’s leader, Jishuka, firing a beautiful arrow. However, even that is not enough to take down Malaxus. Fortunately, Grid’s mana ability has increased significantly , allowing him to display his main-character energy by unleashing his signature Pagma’s Sword Dance and defeating the villain in a perfect closing sequence. Overall, this entire sequence, which lasts around six to seven minutes, is on the level of an animated movie, culminating in a battle where everyone joins forces to take down the main villain, giving their all and risking everything.

This high-quality animation is particularly surprising because this arc isn’t even that major, nor is the anime nearing the conclusion of its season. However, the biggest surprise is that it comes from J.C. Staff, a studio that anime fans had given up on due to its reputation for ruining the One-Punch Man anime . It seems that with Overgeared , J.C. Staff is redeeming its reputation, raising hopes that the finale will be even more epically crafted and further establish the series as Crunchyroll’s hottest Fall 2026 anime, featuring some of the coolest fights this year has to offer.

title: HIDIVE Announces 'Never-Before-Announced New Simulcasts' to Be Revealed at Anime Frontier in Schedule Unveil
content:
Anime streamer HIDIVE announced its schedule for Anime Frontier 2026 across December 4-6, which will be headlined by the upcoming gory yuri title MURCIÉLAGO . Per a press release, the showcase includes seven scheduled events, “ consisting of a trio of premieres, two encore screenings and two panels, including an industry panel that will reveal multiple new acquisitions for the first time publicly .”

The schedule features MURCIÉLAGO , Giant Ojosama , Made in Abyss: Awakening Mystery , Chained Soldier , Nia Liston: The Merciless Maiden , a special guest Q&A with The Dangers in My Heart Producer Kazuki Endo, and “ never-before-announced new simulcasts to be revealed exclusively at Anime Frontier. ” The full schedule and event summaries as stated in the press release (valid as of 11/23) are below. title: Demon Slayer Studio’s Next Big Movie Celebrates Release With New Look Trailer
content:
The studio behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is currently taking over theaters in Japan with a new movie hitting the big screen, and it’s going all out to celebrate the occasion with a new look at Witch on the Holy Night. Studio Ufotable has been keeping very busy over the last couple of years as while fans are waiting to see what’s next for the Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle trilogy , the studio has gone ahead and released a new feature film in the meantime.

Witch on the Holy Night is the next major TYPE-MOON franchise release that Ufotable has helped to bring to life over the last few years, and it’s set before the events of any of the Fate/stay night universe projects seen before. It’s now tearing its way through theaters across Japan, and it’s going all out to commemorate the occasion with a new trailer and poster helping to show it off as it expands to Screen X and other formats in the region. Check them out below.

When Does Witch on the Holy Night Comes Out in the U.S.?

Witch on the Holy Night originally made its debut in Japan this past weekend, but thankfully it won’t be too long before fans in North America get their chance to see it in action for themselves. Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment will be releasing the new film in the United States, Canada and more international territories on January 29th next yea r with both Japanese and English dubbed audio releases planned. If you’ve seen any of the TYPE-MOON projects before, this one is likely going to ring some bells.

Witch on the Holy Night is based off of the TYPE-MOON visual novel originally written by Kinoko Nasu , the same creator behind the massive Fate/stay night franchise. Directed by Masashi Takeuchi for ufotable with Moe Tsuzuki providing the character designs, Manabu Kamino handling the editing, and Hideyuki Fukasawa composing the music, it’s also going to feature the theme song titled “Yoru to Ao” as performed by supercell. Even if you don’t have experience with Nasu’s prior works, this is still a suitable entry point.

What to Know for Witch on the Holy Night

Witch on the Holy Night is a prequel story that takes place before the events of releases like Tsukihime and more that have already gotten their own anime adaptations in the past. The Japanese voice cast from the original light novel release are set to reprise their roles with the likes of Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki, Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji, and Yusuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Shizuki, but the potential English voice cast has yet to be revealed as of this time.

With this story not really tied to anything else, it’s not really going to require any homework to jump into Witch on the Holy Night . Naturally it is going to have a bigger impact on those fans who are experienced with the previously released works, but at least those who just want to see Ufotable’s next movie won’t have to worry too much. Which is even better without a new Demon Slayer entry this year . Are you going to check out Witch on the Holy Night when you get the chance? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Netflix’s One Piece Anime Remake Shares New Look Ahead of 2027 Debut
content:
With only a few months left before the premiere of One Piece ‘s anticipated anime remake, fans get a new look at Luffy and Koby. It’s been almost three years since Netflix’s One Piece remake by WIT Studio was officially announced , and fans have been anticipating the series ever since. The manga began serialization in 1997, and the anime has been ongoing since 1998, making One Piece one of the longest-running franchises of all time. However, beginners would often get overwhelmed with the anime having more than a thousand episodes, which made it even more difficult for the series to get new fans.

The historic success of the live-action adaptation confirmed that anime enthusiasts would be more than willing to follow Luffy’s epic journey if only the series weren’t more than a thousand episodes long. This is why a remake was announced to attract new fans and give the series a modern adaptation . While the anime is still a few months away, ScreenRant shared a new look at Luffy and Koby in an exclusive Winter TV preview. The visual features the duo sailing in a boat, which means it’s set in the time before they ran into Zoro.

Does Netflix’s One Piece Anime Remake Have a Release Date?

The One Piece will premiere with Netflix in February 2027 as part of the Winter 2027 lineup, but the exact release date hasn’t been revealed yet. The One Piece has revealed its teaser , official character designs, and key visuals, but fans still await a full-length trailer featuring everything we need to know before the premiere. We can expect more updates during Jump Festa 2027, which will be held on December 19th and 20th later this year.

As the biggest Shonen Jump manga of all time, One Piece will be holding a panel at the Super Stage where it will drop new updates regarding its ongoing and upcoming projects. Fans can expect more information, including a release date and a trailer for the remake during the convention. The remake will be streaming exclusively on Netflix worldwide, and has already confirmed that the first season will have seven episodes. All of which are expected to drop on the same day.

Netflix’s One Piece Remake Is Solving the Biggest Issues With the Original Anime

The biggest issue fans face in the original anime is the slow pacing, which is caused by the weekly schedule over the years. While the anime adapted a seasonal schedule starting from the Elbaph Arc of the Final Saga, each episode is still adapting only one chapter, which is considerably slow-paced. The remake will adapt the first 50 chapters of the manga in seven episodes, each spanning a little more than 40 minutes. The first season will adapt the East Blue Saga, where Luffy begins his journey and forms a crew to travel all the way to the Grand Line.

The first season will feature up to the Baratie Arc, although it’s uncertain if the entire arc will be covered. At the very least, it’s confirmed that Sanji will be introduced in the first season, along with the rest of the East Blue crew. Additionally, we will need the anime to premiere first before knowing if there will be more seasons going forward. Considering how long One Piece is, the remake will need several more seasons if it plans to adapt the entire story.

title: Naruto’s Live-Action Movie Just Cast the Perfect Third Hokage
content:
A new live-action Naruto feature film is now in the works, and a new report has revealed that the movie has locked down the perfect star as the Third Hokage, Hiruzen Sarutobi. Naruto ‘s new live-action movie is currently slated to fully go in production early next year, and that means we’re about to find out much more about the project. With a worldwide casting search kicking off this year for its three leads , the rest of the cast is steadily coming together as well.

Deadline now reports that Shogun, Mortal Kombat, and John Wick franchise star Hiroyuki Sanada has been cast in the role of the Third Hokage, Hiruzen Sarutobi. The Hokage plays an incredibly important mentor role for Naruto and the rest of the Hidden Leaf Village as they face off against all sorts of threats, and could even see some notable action himself depending on how much the new movie decides to cover in the future .

Hiroyuki Sanada Joins Live-Action Naruto Movie as the Third Hokage

The new Naruto live-action movie is now in the works, but has yet to nail down a concrete release date or window as of this time. Production on the project is set to begin in Spring 2027 with Lionsgate overseeing the production and domestic region release, and Sony Pictures overseeing its international distribution and co-financing. A worldwide casting search began this year for its main trio of Naruto Uzumaki, Sasuke Uchiha, and Sakura Harada, but no casting has been revealed as of this time. Nothing has been officially set in stone.

It’s the same for Charles Melton as Kakashi Hatake, who has been reportedly cast in the new Naruto movie as wel l. But we’ll likely see forward momentum on everything now that we’re so close to the end of the year, and that includes getting a better handle on what kind of materials from Masashi Kishimoto’s original manga the new film will end up using. Various reports have claimed to know what it’s going to cover, but that’s all still a mystery until it officially kicks off its production next year.

What to Know for Naruto ‘s New Live-Action Movie

Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton is coming off of the massive blockbuster success of that film to direct the new live-action Naruto movie for Lionsgate Pictures and Sony Pictures. Cretton is also co-writing the new movie together with Tasha Huo, and is a co-producer alongside Jeyun Munford through Hisako with Avi Arad, Ari Arad and Emmy Yu of Arad Productions. J eremy Latcham was previously attached to the film as a producer before dropping out to become the new head of DC Studios under Skydance.

Reports have teased that the Naruto live-action outing will be taking on the Land of Waves arc of the manga, which was one of Naruto’s first missions as a member of Team 7 . The new film could switch up some things for this new take on the material, but it would serve as a great entry point for this next generation of the franchise. But how are you feeling about Hiroyuki Sanada joining the Naruto movie as the Third Hokage? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

HT – Deadline

title: Dark New Zombie Anime Confirms January 2027 Release Date Ahead of Debut
content:
One of the most anticipated horror anime of 2027 confirms its release date and Japanese broadcast information with a new visual. 2026 is almost nearing its end, which is why the next year’s lineup is revealing all the major information fans can expect. 2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season, which is only a few weeks away. One of the most exciting anime of the season is In a World Full of Zombies I’m the Only One Who Doesn’t Get Attacked , a zombie horror series.

There has been a shortage of zombie movies in the industry for quite some time, even though Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead was quite a massive hit in 2023. However, this new zombie series is expected to be the next big hit. The official X handle of the anime confirmed that AT-X on Friday, January 1, 2027, at 1:00 a.m. JST. The streaming platform hasn’t been revealed yet, but we can expect an update before the end of the year. Along with the broadcast information, the handle post also includes an older visual featuring the central characters.

What Is In a World Full of Zombies I’m the Only One Who Doesn’t Get Attacked About?

The anime is based on a light novel series of the same name written by Rokuro Uraji and illustrated by Saburo. The story centers around an ordinary office worker, Yusuke, who dislikes people and prefers to do his job in silence. However, when the company he was employed at goes bankrupt, he loses his job and becomes a shut-in with no motivation to work again. On a rare day, he leaves his apartment after playing video games for a week but never expected a mysterious man to bite his arm.

While Yusuke avoids getting hurt anymore, he becomes bedridden with a fever, never expecting the world would change when he was asleep. He sees that zombies have emerged in every corner of the world and only a few humans have survived the apocalypse. For some reason, he is the only one who isn’t getting attacked by zombies, and it might be related to his unexpected encounter with the man who bit him.

This Upcoming New Zombie Anime Might Be the Next Big Hit

A zombie apocalypse is one of those premises that fans will always love, especially those who have been starving for a horror genre. With the anime being oversaturated with battle action that centers around supernatural power systems or isekai fantasies, horror shows have become quite a rarity. This is especially the case for shows centering around Zombies since the last time a major hit was released was more than three years ago.

Not only that, but this upcoming series also comes with its own set of mysteries and plot twists that set it apart from any ordinary horror show. The anime has yet to reveal any information regarding its global streaming, but we can expect any major platform such as Crunchyroll, Netflix, or HIDIVE to pick it up soon.

Are you excited to watch this upcoming zombie horror series? Do you think it could have the same appeal as the major shows of 2027? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Dragon Ball Super Remake Is Already Setting Up Ultra Instinct’s Debut
content:
Dragon Ball Super ‘s new remake has officially kicked off the Resurrection F arc with its latest episode, and Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has also planted the first seeds for Ultra Instinct Goku’s big debut. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is a newly enhanced version of the now classic TV anime series, and with the benefit of retrospect has been able to fine tune how each of the episodes play out knowing what’s next to come in the future. That’s what makes its newest addition all the more interesting.

Dragon Ball Super fans know that the anime eventually reaches its climax with the full debut of Mastered Ultra Instinct Goku , and Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been able to use that to start planting the seeds for it much sooner than usual. Because while the anime hasn’t really changed any of the audio or story sequences from the original, it’s been able to add a new visual flourish to help set up Ultra Instinct’s eventually debut with the latest episode.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 7 Teases Ultra Instinct

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 7 kicks off the Resurrection F arc with Goku and Vegeta training with Whis on Beerus’ planet . This training segment is extended beyond what was seen in the original version as well as the conversation that Whis has with the two of them about their strengths and weaknesses. When Whis tells them they will need to train their body to move before they even think of those movements, the new version now adds a flair of silver aura that wasn’t in the original. It’s because now the team knows what Ultra Instinct already looks like.

Rather than like the first time around where the Dragon Ball Super anime production team were kind of figuring things out alongside Akira Toriyama as the series developed, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is able to use those future events to foreshadow them much sooner than before. It makes for a more complete experience for those new audiences who are just jumping into the anime with this new edition, and will hopefully make Ultra Instinct that much more explosive if/when the remake eventually gets to the Tournament of Power.

What Does This Mean for Dragon Ball Super’ s Remake Anime Future?

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has only been confirmed to enhance the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs before it comes to an end. It’s yet to be revealed as to whether or not the Future Trunks and Universe Survival arcs are going to get the remake treatment next, but that seems likely given that these three arcs have gone through the trouble of being reinterpreted in this way. That’s going to be even more necessary to bridge the gap to the Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol anime at some point too.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been divisive thus far with the number of changes it has made to the classic TV anime, and the lack of new additions seen with the episodes so far . But with foreshadowing like this to help make the package seemed like it was all planned out from the start, it’s going to make this new version the most complete version of the story. But how are you feeling about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Re:Zero Star Breaks Silence on Anime’s Future After Season 5
content:
The voice behind Subaru Natsuki finally shared the anime’s future even after Season 5. 2026 was a major year for Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World – fans, as the anime not only aired its fourth season, but also commemorated its 10th anniversary. The fifth season has already been confirmed, and it’s going to be more intense than ever. The anime is based on an ongoing novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichirou Otsuka. As one of the biggest shows on Crunchyroll, it’s no surprise Re:Zero was renewed for a fifth season not long after the fourth season finale.

The story is currently at a crucial phase as Subaru Natsuki was forced to witness his friends die in gruesome ways, forcing him to realize his weakness. Fans are more excited to see his journey continue in Season 5, especially after Rem woke up from her coma. During the anime’s 10th anniversary event last week, the voice actors were in attendance and discussed their experiences working on the series for a decade. The anime has only just confirmed its fifth season, but Yusuke Kobayashi, the voice behind Natsuki Subaru, already revealed what to expect from the anime going forward.

Re:Zero Voice Actor Confirms the Anime Will Run For a Long Time

Mantan Web shares his speech during the event, where Kobayashi says, “This toast is not a toast to a milestone, but the first call to continue running. We will continue to run for a long time to come, so we would be happy if you would continue to support and run with us in the world of Re:Zero , which may continue for decades to come.”

Since the novel is ongoing, it goes without saying that the fifth season won’t be able to adapt the entire story. Since the anime is already popular, fans will keep getting sequel seasons until the story is over. Kobayashi’s closing remarks during the event confirm that the anime has a long future ahead, which may even continue for decades. In February this year, Nagatsuki confirmed that the novel’s story is only halfway over after 14 years of serialization. This means the anime will keep releasing more seasons for another decade or even more.

Re:Zero Season 5 Will Be More Brutal Than Ever

During the Season 5 announcement, Nagatsuki shared a special message to fans while dropping major hints about what to expect from the anime. While the creator didn’t drop any major spoilers, he revealed that the but the journey from here on out will be even more grueling than ever, even comparing it to an inferno.

Season 4 was already a brutal journey , but Subaru won’t be able to catch a break in the upcoming season as well. Nagatsuki also assures fans that the journey from here on out won’t be all about hardship. Fans can also look forward to new encounters and exciting developments, which means we can expect new character introductions in Season 5 as well.

What are you most excited to see in the anime’s Season 5? What do you hope will happen next in Subaru’s journey? Share your thoughts in the comments below!
